Mini Pumpkins — Cozy Fall Mini Pumpkins 🎃

These mini pumpkins have been my go-to for fall tables — soft, quick to make, and those little brown stems with curly vines make me smile every time I see them.

Hey, it's Sara. I made these four mini pumpkins on a golden October afternoon with the window open and warm amber light coming in — real pumpkins on my table, cinnamon sticks and pinecones around, and a cup of tea steaming beside me. A friend asked for table decor that wasn't plastic — something that looks real — so I sat at my wooden table with burnt orange, cream, mustard, and rust yarn and crocheted four little pumpkins while my tea went cold. By sunset I had four cozy pumpkins, each about 2.5 inches wide, on my wooden crate. This is the long beginner version where I explain what's happening between each step, with progress photos for every stage.

Level Beginner — cozy & quick — about 40 minutes per pumpkin — first amigurumi ball
Yarn Worsted / medium weight — about 9g per pumpkin — roughly 36g for a set of four — plus a little brown and green — 4mm hook
Size Pumpkin about 2.5" wide ×1.5" tall — stem 0.8" tall — vine 3" curled — gauge 18 sc = 4"

Before you begin

I've been wanting mini pumpkins that feel like a warm hug for fall, and these four turned out exactly like that. The burnt orange, cream, mustard, and rust remind me of leaves and pumpkins at the farm, and the worsted stitches make them cozy without being too heavy.

What I love about this pattern is how fast it works up. Because we are using worsted yarn and a 4mm hook, the fabric grows quickly — perfect if you want to make a set today and style them tomorrow morning with your tea.

Tip from my table: Stuff lightly but enough to hold the shape. A little firm at first is good — worsted relaxes after a day or two — so light-firm stuffing keeps them from going flat. About 4 to 5 grams of polyfill per 2.5-inch pumpkin is plenty. For the ridges, pull gently — if you pull too hard the pumpkin flattens.

Materials I used

MATERIALS:
Worsted / medium weight yarn: About 36g total for 4 pumpkins — about 9g per pumpkin — I used burnt orange, cream, mustard, and rust — each from a 50g / 100m skein — roughly 9m per pumpkin
Brown yarn for stems: About 6g total — roughly 1.5g per stem — 4 stems
Green yarn for vines: About 6g total — roughly 1.5g per vine — 4 vines
4mm crochet hook — keeps fabric tight so polyfill doesn't show
Polyfill: About 18g total — 4 to 5g per pumpkin — light stuffing
Yarn needle, scissors, stitch marker, tape measure
Optional for photos: cinnamon sticks, pinecones, dried leaves, wooden crate

Sizing & how to measure

SIZING:
Finished pumpkin: About 2.5" wide ×1.5" tall without stem — stem 0.8" tall — vine 3" curled
At a gauge of 18 sc = 4", 36 stitches gives about 8" around, which is about 2.5" across — that matches the size stated.
To check, measure across the widest point — it should be about 2.5". If yours is 2", try a 4.5mm hook. If it's 3", try a 3.5mm hook.

Abbreviations

ABBREVIATIONS — US terms:
ch = chain, sc = single crochet, inc = increase — 2 sc in same stitch, dec = decrease — sc2tog, MR = magic ring, st(s) = stitch(es), sl st = slip stitch

Full roadmap — 6 steps

FULL ROADMAP — 6 STEPS:
1. Magic ring to widest — 6 to 36 stitches — about 2.5" wide
2. Body — straight rounds at 36 stitches — 6 rounds — about 1.2" tall
3. Closing — 36 down to 6 — stuff with 4 to 5g — leave a 24" tail for ridges
4. Ridges — wrap 6 times — 6 sections like a real pumpkin
5. Stem — brown tube — 0.8" tall
6. Vine — green curly vine — chain 20, 2 sc in each chain — 38 sc — about 3" curled

Step 1 — Magic ring to widest — 6 to 36 — 2.5" wide

Hey, it's Sara here — what's happening in Step 1:
We are starting your pumpkin with a magic ring because it closes with no hole. We grow from 6 stitches to 36 over six rounds. This sets the width of the whole pumpkin — about 2.5 inches. Place a marker in the first stitch of each round and count out loud — I do — and sip your tea as you go.
Step 1 — starting with a magic ring, growing to 36 stitches — about 2.5 inches wide
STEP 1:
R1: MR, 6 sc — 6
R2: inc ×6 — 12
R3: (sc, inc) ×6 — 18
R4: (sc 2, inc) ×6 — 24 — about 1.5" wide
R5: (sc 3, inc) ×6 — 30 — about 2" wide
R6: (sc 4, inc) ×6 — 36 — about 2.5" wide — 36 stitches

Step 2 — Body — straight — 36 stitches ×6 rounds — 1.2" tall

Sara here — what's happening in Step 2:
Now we stop increasing and go straight up. 36 stitches around for six rounds — no increases, no decreases. This builds the height — about 1.2 inches. It will start to look like a little bowl. This is the coziest part because it grows fast and you can see the pumpkin shape coming. Keep your tension even.
Step 2 — body — 36 stitches around for 6 rounds — about 1.2 inches tall — bowl shape forming
STEP 2:
R7-12: sc 36 around ×6 rounds — 36 sc each round — about 1.2" tall — straight sides

Step 3 — Closing — 36 down to 6 — stuff lightly

Sara here — what's happening in Step 3:
We close the pumpkin. We go from 36 down to 6 with gentle decreases. At 18 stitches, stuff with about 4 to 5 grams of polyfill — just enough to hold shape, not rock hard. Keep decreasing to 6, close with a needle, pull tight, and leave a long 24-inch tail for the ridges.
Step 3 — after closing — each pumpkin holds its shape with light stuffing — about 4 to 5 grams per pumpkin
STEP 3:
R13: (sc 4, dec) ×6 — 30
R14: (sc 3, dec) ×6 — 24
R15: (sc 2, dec) ×6 — 18 — stuff with 4 to 5g polyfill now
R16: (sc, dec) ×6 — 12
R17: dec ×6 — 6 — close — pull yarn through remaining 6 stitches — leave a 24" tail for ridges

Step 4 — Ridges — 6 sections like a real pumpkin

Sara here — my favorite — what's happening in Step 4:
This is where a plain ball becomes a pumpkin. Thread the long tail in your yarn needle, go from bottom center to top center, wrap around the outside, back through bottom to top, and pull gently for a ridge. Repeat six times around — six wraps makes six sections, just like a real pumpkin. Pull gently — if you pull too hard the pumpkin flattens.
Step 4 — wrapping the long tail six times to form six soft ridges — gentle pull keeps the pumpkin puffy
STEP 4:
Thread the 24" tail in needle — go from bottom center to top center — wrap around outside — back through bottom to top — pull gently — repeat 6 times around — 6 sections — tie at bottom — weave in — pumpkin about 2.5" wide ×1.5" tall with 6 ridges

Step 5 — Stem — brown — 0.8" tall

Sara here — what's happening in Step 5:
Now the little brown stem — a tiny tube. Magic ring 6, then three rounds of 6 sc — about 0.8 inches tall. Sew it on top center where all the ridges meet — three or four stitches. Brown yarn looks like a real stem.
STEP 5:
R1: MR, 6 sc — 6
R2-4: sc 6 around ×3 rounds — 6 sc — about 0.8" tall tube
Fasten off, leave an 8" tail — sew on top center — 3 to 4 stitches

Step 6 — Vine — green curly — 3" curled

Sara here — last step — what's happening in Step 6:
Last little touch — a curly vine. Chain 20, then 2 sc in each chain — that's 38 sc — it curls by itself to about 3 inches. Sew it next to the stem with one stitch. If you want it longer, chain 25 for about 4 inches curled, but 20 is perfect for mini.
Finished set — four mini pumpkins — burnt orange, cream, mustard, rust — each about 2.5 inches wide with brown stem and green curly vine — styled on a wooden crate with fall leaves
STEP 6:
Ch 20
Row 1: 2 sc in 2nd ch from hook and in each ch across — 38 sc — curls naturally — about 3" curled
Fasten off, leave a 6" tail — sew next to stem — 1 stitch

How I finish mine, ways to make it your own, and caring

Sara — how I finish mine:
I weave ends in with a yarn needle, going through the bottom a couple times so they don't pop out. Worsted can be a little slippery, so I go an extra inch or two. For photos I like to place pumpkins on a wooden crate with pinecones, cinnamon sticks, and fall leaves.
WAYS TO MAKE IT YOUR OWN:
Color play: Cream with brown stem, mustard with rust, oatmeal, pumpkin, rust, mustard, chocolate — warm fall palette — mixed set of four looks cozy
No vine: Leave the vine off for a minimal look — just the stem — still cute
Bigger pumpkin — about 3" wide: To make a slightly larger pumpkin, add one more increase round: (sc 5, inc) ×6 — 42 stitches — then work 8 rounds straight at 42 — then close 42 to 36 to 30 to 24 to 18 to 12 to 6 — about 3" wide at same gauge — not 3.5"
Smaller pumpkin — about 1.5" wide: Stop at 24 stitches — (sc 2, inc) ×6 =24 — work 3 rounds straight at 24 — then close 24→18→12→6 — cute for tiered trays
Add a leaf: Crochet a small leaf in green and sew near the stem for extra fall

I spot clean mine gently with a little cool water and pat dry, then lay flat. Fluff with fingers after — keeps shape nice. Store in a basket, not squished, so ridges keep their shape.

  • Ridges: Wrap tail 6 times — 6 sections — 2.5" wide ×1.5" tall
